Subject: Vendor cascade + DPA annex — proposed edits

Marissa,

Thanks again for the call this morning. As discussed, we ran your MSA + Order Form against FleetOps' standard procurement guardrails. Procurement flagged two items that require contractual language alignment before we can proceed to signature: (1) the next-tier subprocessor flow-down (we need explicit obligations and an audit clause); and (2) the DPA annex — data transfer dependencies and subprocessors list are out of sync with what was provided in your portal.

I've attached a consolidated redline (FleetOps_proposed_cascade_redline_v1.docx) that merges our procurement team's preferred language and the DPA annex edits. High level asks:
- Add a short auditing right for FleetOps to validate third-party subprocessors (90 days notice, limited scope).
- Ensure all subcontracting requires prior written consent for any subprocessors that access production data.
- Clarify data export regions and reference the DPA annex as the definitive source for subprocessors.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept the audit scope language, or if you prefer Redwood's alternate (described in the comments). If we can align on the cascade paragraph and the DPA annex reference, procurement can clear signature and we will route to legal for final DocuSign.

Best,

Subject: RE: Vendor cascade + DPA annex — proposed edits

Team — I reviewed FleetOps' suggested redline and the DPA annex. Summary and recommended positions below (tracked in attached DPA_annex_track_changes.pdf):

1) Audit right: Accept in principle but narrow the scope. Proposed language: "Customer may request a single, vendor-provided evidence package and, subject to confidentiality obligations, may conduct one on-site or remote audit per 12 months focused solely on controls directly related to the Services and Customer Data. Vendor will respond within 30 days to remediate any confirmed findings." This gives a single annual right, limits scope, and avoids broad sysadmin-level access.

2) Prior written consent for subprocessors: We should accept for any party that accesses Customer Data (PII or production content). For non-data subprocessors (e.g., facilities, courier) propose an exception. Also propose a standard notification window (15 business days) for additions to the subprocessors list with an objection window of 20 business days.

3) DPA annex canonical reference: We should accept language that the DPA annex governs data transfers, but must preserve Redwood's right to update subprocessors in the portal and notify customers. Add an explicit process to escalate disagreements to legal teams before procurement termination remedies.

Action items:
- Priyom: prepare counter-redline that incorporates the audit wording above and the object/notify timeline for subprocessors (target EOD today).
- Karthik: confirm whether procurement needs an additional insurance or SLA callout (they asked about retention liability).
- Marissa: once Priyom drops the counter-redline, I'll share with FleetOps with rationale.

Attachment: DPA_annex_track_changes.pdf

Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
